core_obligations: Use the characterisation of weak adicness and the earlier result on the completed tensor product to obtain admissibility and an ideal of definition given by the closure of the sum of the two extended ideals of definition (proof lines 1762-1770).

Show that the closures of the powers of that ideal are open, by the containment of the nth power in the sum of the ideals generated by the nth powers of the two given ideals and by openness of those closures in the two rings (proof lines 1770-1777).
proof_roadmap: Admissibility and the ideal of definition (proof lines 1762-1770).
Openness of the closures of the powers (proof lines 1770-1777).
difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms of linearly topologized rings, the lemma asserts that the completed tensor product of two weakly pre-adic rings is weakly adic (statement lines 1755-1760). The proof uses the characterisation of weak adicness and the earlier analysis of the completed tensor product: that analysis gives admissibility of the completed tensor product, and its proof shows that the closure of the sum of the ideals generated by ideals of definition of the two rings is an ideal of definition (proof lines 1762-1770). It therefore remains to see that the closures of the powers of that ideal are open, which follows because the nth power contains the sum of the ideals generated by the nth powers of the two given ideals, and those closures are open by the hypothesis that the two rings are weakly pre-adic (proof lines 1770-1777). The claim is H2: the argument reuses the proof of the preceding lemma for the ideal of definition and then verifies the second half of the characterisation by a containment of powers, so it is short but complete and not a restatement.
